title: GPT-4o Lacks Core Features of Theory of Mind

model.params_source: paper 'LLM Used' ('We left parameters at their default values: temperature=1 and top_p=1 ... we set response_format=json'); logprobs/top_logprobs are ours - the paper reads 'the LLM's probability distribution over next tokens (e.g. "box" or "basket")', which needs logprobs, but does not say how many were requested. max_tokens 256 is ours.

task.subset_rule: all 243 ContainerWorld tuples: every combination of beliefs B, desires D and states S (9 x 3 x 9, Procedure)
task.approximation: blocked: the verbatim prompts are on OSF and the comparison model is not printed (see open_points). Item construction from the text alone (spawn corner, box next to the character, covered basket 'about 50 steps away', fruit sets {apples, oranges, apples and oranges}, desires {like, dislike} with not both disliked, closing question 'Which container would Jason open?') would be our own wording.

items.source: OSF repository of the paper, https://osf.io/8eha3/ ('Code and data for this paper can be found at the accompanying OSF repository'); the vignettes are generated combinatorially, so the materials are the generator plus the system/user prompts
items.license: unknown (OSF node not readable from here)

download.check: https://osf.io/8eha3/ returns 200 but only the OSF single-page-app shell; api.osf.io/v2/nodes/8eha3/ and /files/osfstorage/ return 401 Unauthorized and files.osf.io/v1/resources/8eha3/providers/osfstorage/ returns 403 from this machine, so the file list, the prompts and the licence could not be read.

prompt.system: [not printed] a system prompt 'informing the LLM of its task and providing a JSON schema informing the LLM how to structure its response' (Procedure); available on OSF
prompt.user_template: [not printed] parametrically generated transcription of <beliefs, desires, states>, always ending with the question “Which container would Jason open?”
prompt.source_location: Methods / Procedure ('all system and user prompts are available on OSF'); Figure 2A shows one rendered ContainerWorld instance as an illustration
prompt.verbatim: partial: only the closing question is quoted in the text. The system prompt, the JSON schema and the vignette template are on OSF, which could not be read (see items.download).

output.postprocess: the paper does not parse the text: it takes the next-token probability distribution over 'box' and 'basket' as the model's action distribution
output.parse_paper: probability distribution over the next token ('box' vs 'basket') from the logprobs

metric.name: custom
metric.definition: % Agreement between GPT-4o's predicted action and the HumanToM candidate model's prediction over the 243 ContainerWorld tuples (87.24% = 212/243). HumanToM is the full belief-desire-cost utility model of Jara-Ettinger et al. (2016); the ablated candidates (BeliefDesire 27.98, Belief 0, DesireCost 65.84, Desire 0, Cost 74.07) come from the same family.
metric.judge: none (agreement with a computational model, not with a gold label)
metric.original_location: Figure 1C ('Accuracy on ContainerWorld'), bar HumanToM, printed value 87.24

cost.prepare_note: not run: no prompts and no gold predictions.

open_points: prompts: the system prompt, the JSON schema and the user-vignette template are only on OSF (https://osf.io/8eha3/), and the OSF API is not reachable from this machine (401/403). Until the node's files can be read, the prompt cannot be copied verbatim.

gold: '% Agreement' is agreement with the HumanToM model's own predictions, and that model (utility = desire x state minus cost, with the paper's cost/softmax parameters) is described but not parameterised in the text. Its 243 predictions have to come from the OSF code; re-deriving them would be our own model.

scoring input: the paper scores the next-token probability distribution, not the parsed answer. The runner archives the full API record, but hook score() sees only parsed predictions, so a logprob-based comparison needs a runner change (or a score_with_judge-style hook that reads the archive).
notes: 243 = 9 belief x 3 desire x 9 state tuples; 87.24% is exactly 212/243, i.e. the agreement is counted per tuple. The MovieWorld replication (Study 3) and the mental-state inference correlations use the same materials and have the same blockers. Even with the OSF files this stays a three-part reconstruction (prompt, candidate model, logprob scoring), so it is a needs_human rather than a needs_download_check.
